children: An Anthropic insider has delivered a bleak warning from inside the AI industry. Evan Hubinger, the company's alignment science lead, said he earnestly believes AI could kill every human, placing the probability above 10% within the next decade.
The statement is Hubinger's personal estimate, not Anthropic's official forecast. The warning is striking because his job is preventing dangerous behavior by increasingly capable systems.
Anthropic's Official Assessment Is Less Dire

Hubinger said Anthropic is trying its best, but lacks a clear plan for aligning superintelligence and is not clearly on track to solve the problem. The warning accompanies Anthropic's latest risk report, which acknowledges mounting uncertainty.

-backed Anthropic currently rates catastrophic danger from known forms of model misalignment as low, up from very low. The company has observed models showing willingness to take misaligned actions, but says current safeguards and limited covert capabilities keep catastrophic risk contained.

Unknown failure modes are harder to measure. Anthropic considers severe, pervasive unknown misalignment very unlikely, while admitting that its ability to evaluate future systems remains limited. That gap explains why Hubinger can hold a much darker long-term view than the company's present operational rating.

Automated research creates another pressure point. Anthropic says its models already accelerate internal AI development, though not yet twofold. Some capability tests have saturated, reducing confidence in existing measurements, while early evidence suggests AI-driven research acceleration is emerging.

The company believes automated research risk could become a major concern within six to 12 months. For investors, policymakers and users, the key distinction is timing: Anthropic sees current catastrophic risk as low, while its own alignment lead believes rapidly improving systems could create an existential threat within the next ten years. This is not proof that disaster is inevitable. It is a warning that the people building frontier AI still lack confidence that control will scale alongside capability.

title: Anthropic Insider Drops Chilling AI Extinction Warning
